items.q: What is quick commerce and which platforms matter in India?
a: Quick commerce (q-commerce) is the delivery of groceries, FMCG, beauty and everyday products in roughly 10–30 minutes from local dark stores. In India the platforms that matter are Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy Instamart, Flipkart Minutes, Amazon Now and BigBasket (BB Now).
gaa-tha onboards brands onto all of them and runs the catalogue, availability, ads and ratings as one operation.

items.q: What does a quick commerce agency do?
a: A quick commerce agency gets a brand listed on 10-minute delivery platforms and then runs the account: catalogue and thumbnails, city and dark-store availability, purchase orders and replenishment, promotions and ads, ratings and monthly reporting.
We do this for Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy Instamart, Flipkart Minutes, Amazon Now and BigBasket from one team, with one monthly report.

items.q: Which quick commerce platform should I launch on first?
a: Start where your category and your target cities overlap best. Blinkit and Zepto lead metro grocery and FMCG; Swiggy Instamart is strong on food and impulse categories; BigBasket suits staples and larger packs; Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now are expanding city by city.
We map your SKUs, margins and cities against each platform's category demand and recommend an order before you apply anywhere.

items.q: How long does Blinkit, Zepto or Instamart onboarding take?
a: Typically two to six weeks from application to first purchase order, depending on category approvals, documentation and how quickly catalogue and images are ready. Food and beauty categories with licence checks take longer than packaged non-food.
We prepare the documents, catalogue and images in parallel so the platform review is the only wait.

items.q: What documents do I need to sell on Blinkit or Zepto?
a: Usually GST registration, brand ownership proof or a brand authorisation letter, bank account details, a trademark certificate or application where available, and category licences such as FSSAI for food. Product data — barcodes, MRP, pack sizes, shelf life, dimensions — is needed for the catalogue.
Requirements change by platform and category, so we share a current checklist before you apply.

items.q: Are there fees to get listed on quick commerce platforms?
a: Platforms work on a margin per SKU and may have onboarding, listing or marketing contributions; these vary by category and change over time, and some are negotiable at scale.
We share the current structure for your category before you sign and plan pack sizes and pricing so the margin works after platform costs.

items.q: What is marketplace account management?
a: Marketplace account management is the ongoing operation of a brand's seller account on platforms like Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra and Nykaa: listings and A+ content, pricing and deals, sponsored ads, inventory and fulfilment planning, account health, reviews and monthly reporting.
gaa-tha runs it as a monthly retainer with a named account manager and a P&L-style report.

items.q: Do you handle Amazon and Flipkart onboarding?
a: Yes. Seller registration, Brand Registry or brand approval, category approvals, catalogue creation, A+ content, Brand Store and a go-live checklist — then optional monthly account management.
Fashion and beauty brands can add Myntra, Nykaa and AJIO; price-led categories can add Meesho and JioMart.

items.q: Can you manage D2C, marketplaces and quick commerce together?
a: Yes — that is the point of the practice. One team handles your Shopify store, Amazon and Flipkart accounts and Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart listings, so pricing, pack sizes, content and promotions stay consistent across every channel.
You get one monthly report showing revenue and margin by channel rather than three agencies with three versions of the truth.

items.q: Do you build and manage Shopify stores?
a: Yes. We design and develop Shopify stores — custom themes and sections, checkout and payment integrations, COD and pincode rules, Meta Pixel and Conversions API, GA4 — and run monthly store management for product uploads, price changes, banners, apps and fixes.
Migrations from Amazon or WooCommerce are included in scope where needed.

items.q: Can one website serve multiple store locations or franchises?
a: Yes. A multi-location Shopify build lets the customer enter a pincode or choose an outlet; the order is routed to that outlet with a WhatsApp notification, and each outlet can have its own availability, delivery rules and prepaid/COD settings on one shared catalogue and price list.
It suits retail chains, franchises, sweet and snack stores and local delivery brands.

items.q: How do you price ecommerce and quick commerce services?
a: Onboarding is a one-time project fee per platform. Ongoing work — account management, store management, ads — is a monthly retainer scoped to the number of platforms, SKUs and cities. Ad spend is paid by you directly to the platform, with no markup.
We send a written scope and price within 48 hours of the first call.

items.q: How do you measure success on marketplaces?
a: Orders, revenue and net margin after fees and returns; advertising ACoS/TACoS; organic rank for target keywords; conversion rate; ratings and review count; and account health. On quick commerce we add availability and fill rate by city.
All of it is reported monthly against the targets agreed at the start.

items.q: My listings are live but not selling — can you fix that?
a: Usually. Stalled listings almost always have one of four problems: weak titles and images, no reviews, uncompetitive pricing, or no advertising. We audit the account, fix content and pricing, set up sponsored ads and a compliant review process, and track rank and conversion weekly.
If the problem is availability — out of stock or not live in the right cities — we fix that first.

items.q: Do you create product images and A+ content?
a: Yes. White-background packshots, lifestyle scenes, infographic 'why buy' images, pack-size visuals and A+ or enhanced-content modules, made to each platform's specs — with AI-assisted shoots for large catalogues so 200-SKU ranges do not take months.
Quick-commerce thumbnails are treated as their own format: they have to win in a two-second scroll.

items.q: Do you make cinema ads?
a: Yes. Trailer-grade 10, 20 and 30-second films cut for cinema screens, OTT, YouTube and in-store displays — produced live-action or with AI and human art direction, delivered in 2.39:1 scope and vertical versions.
They work best for retail chains, FMCG launches and festive campaigns that need city-wide recall.

items.q: Do you generate B2B and export leads for manufacturers?
a: Yes. LinkedIn outreach to named decision-makers, Meta and LinkedIn lead ads, IndiaMART and TradeIndia listing optimisation, WhatsApp first-reply templates and a lead-qualification SOP with a tracker your sales team will actually use.
It is built for manufacturers, exporters, packaging, machinery and bulk food suppliers.

items.q: Can we see results from similar brands?
a: Yes. Our case studies are published one by one as each client approves them and the numbers are confirmed from real reports — we do not publish estimates. Browse what is live on the work page, and ask us for a walkthrough of unpublished work in your category on a call.
Every case study lists the services used and links to those service pages.

items.q: Do you work with manufacturers, FMCG, retail, real estate and education brands?
a: Yes. Current and past clients include packaged-snack and FMCG brands, sweets and gifting retailers, machinery, coatings and packaging manufacturers, a co-living brand, an overseas-education consultancy and a D2C skincare brand.
The process is the same across industries; the channels and references change.

items.q: Do you work with international clients?
a: Yes. We work remotely-first with brands outside India — including a trading-card and hobbies retailer in Canada — on social content, creative, copy and websites. On-ground shoots are arranged locally where needed.
Time zones are handled with a shared calendar and weekly reviews.

items.q: What are the best Shopify features for an ecommerce store?
a: The Shopify features that matter most for a growing ecommerce store are its reliable hosted checkout, the theme editor with sections on every page, metafields and metaobjects for rich product data, native discounts and bundles, customer segments, Shopify Flow automations and the Search & Discovery app for filters and recommendations.

Add the app ecosystem for payments, shipping, reviews and WhatsApp, and a small team can run a serious store without a developer on call. gaa-tha sets these up as part of every Shopify build so they are actually used, not just available.

items.q: What hidden Shopify features should I try?
a: The most under-used Shopify features are metaobjects for reusable content such as ingredient or size-guide libraries, Shopify Flow for free automations like order tagging and low-stock alerts, bulk URL redirect import, customer segments for targeted Shopify Email campaigns and discounts, draft orders for phone and WhatsApp sales, and the Search & Discovery app for synonyms, filters and product boosts.
Many stores pay for apps that duplicate something Shopify already does natively, so an audit of these features often cuts app costs as well as adding capability.

items.q: What is the right budget to build a Shopify website in India?
a: As an indicative 2026 Indian market range (not a quote), a template-based Shopify store set up by a freelancer typically costs ₹25,000–₹75,000, a customised store from an agency ₹75,000–₹3 lakh, and a custom-designed theme with complex features ₹3–10 lakh or more, with Shopify Plus and headless builds going higher.

On top of the build, budget for the monthly Shopify plan, paid apps, payment-gateway fees per transaction and ongoing store management. The number moves with design originality, catalogue size, integrations such as checkout, shipping and ERP, and content like photography and copy.

items.q: Is Shopify a good platform for ecommerce in India?
a: Yes — Shopify is one of the most practical ecommerce platforms for Indian D2C brands because it is hosted, secure and fast to launch, and it works with Indian payment gateways, COD, UPI, shipping aggregators like Shiprocket and GST invoicing apps.

The main India-specific caveat is that Shopify Payments and Shop Pay are not generally available to Indian-registered stores, so checkout runs through gateways such as Razorpay, PayU, Cashfree or CCAvenue, or one-click checkouts such as GoKwik, Shiprocket Checkout and Razorpay Magic Checkout. For multi-vendor marketplaces or complex B2B portals, a custom build can be the better fit.

items.q: Shopify vs WooCommerce vs a custom-built store — which should I choose?
a: Choose Shopify if you want to sell quickly with low maintenance, WooCommerce if you already run WordPress and want full control of hosting and plugins, and a custom build only when your model — a multi-vendor marketplace, complex B2B pricing or unusual workflows — genuinely does not fit a platform.

Shopify charges a monthly fee but removes hosting, security and update work; WooCommerce is cheaper to start but needs ongoing maintenance; custom code costs the most to build and to own. For most Indian D2C brands, Shopify is the default and the others are exceptions.

items.q: Can Shopify integrate with Razorpay, Shiprocket, WhatsApp, Tally and Amazon or Flipkart?
a: Yes — Shopify connects to Razorpay and other Indian gateways for payments, to Shiprocket and similar aggregators for shipping, and to WhatsApp Business API tools for order updates and abandoned-cart messages, mostly through ready-made apps.

Tally, Amazon and Flipkart usually need a connector app or custom middleware to sync orders, inventory and invoices, and the right option depends on order volume and how your accounts team works. gaa-tha scopes and builds these integrations so stock and orders match across every channel.

items.q: Does Shopify support Cash on Delivery and UPI in India?
a: Yes — Shopify supports Cash on Delivery as a built-in manual payment method, and UPI, cards, net banking and wallets through Indian gateways such as Razorpay, PayU, Cashfree and PhonePe.

Most Indian stores also add COD controls — pincode serviceability, order-value limits, COD fees or partial prepaid, and OTP or WhatsApp confirmation — to cut return-to-origin losses. One-click checkouts such as GoKwik and Shiprocket Checkout bring these controls and prepaid nudges together in one place.

items.q: How long does it take to build a Shopify store?
a: A Shopify store typically takes 3–6 weeks for a customised theme with a modest catalogue, and 8–14 weeks for a custom-designed theme with integrations, a migration or a large catalogue.

The biggest delays are rarely development — they are product data, photography, copy and payment-gateway approvals, so gaa-tha starts those in parallel with design. A realistic launch date is agreed in the written scope before work begins.

items.q: Can you migrate my store to Shopify without losing SEO rankings?
a: Yes — a Shopify migration can keep your search rankings if every old URL is mapped to its new Shopify URL with a 301 redirect, and titles, meta descriptions, structured data and content are carried over before launch.

Shopify uses fixed URL patterns (/products/, /collections/, /pages/, /blogs/), so redirects are essential when moving from WooCommerce, Magento, Wix or a custom site. gaa-tha migrates products, customers and order history, then monitors Google Search Console after launch to catch 404s and ranking dips early.

items.q: Is Shopify Plus worth it?
a: Shopify Plus is worth it when a brand has outgrown the standard plans — high order volumes, checkout customisation, B2B wholesale pricing, multiple expansion stores, higher API limits or advanced automation — and those features save or earn more than the higher fee costs.

Plus is priced well above the standard plans, so check Shopify’s current pricing and compare it with what you spend today on apps, workarounds and lost conversions. Many Indian brands are better served by a well-built standard Shopify store until volume justifies the move.

items.q: What is headless Shopify and do I need it?
a: Headless Shopify means Shopify runs products, inventory, checkout and orders in the back end while the storefront is a separately built front end, usually made with Shopify Hydrogen or Next.js using the Storefront API.

It gives complete design freedom, very fast pages and the ability to blend content from other systems, but it costs more to build and maintain than a theme. Most brands do not need it; it makes sense for content-heavy brands, complex multi-region storefronts or teams with in-house developers.

items.q: Who is the best Shopify agency in India, and how do I choose one?
a: There is no single best Shopify agency in India — the right one is the type that matches your stage: a freelancer for a simple template store, a Shopify-only studio for design-heavy builds, or a full-service agency when you also need branding, content, ads and marketplace management.

Ask to see live stores they built, who will actually work on yours, whether the store and accounts stay in your name, how they handle Indian payments, COD and shipping, and what monthly support costs after launch. gaa-tha is a full-service agency, so we suit brands that want the store and the growth work under one team.

items.q: How much does a website cost in India?
a: As an indicative 2026 Indian market range (not a quote), a simple template website typically costs ₹15,000–₹60,000, a custom-designed business or brand website ₹60,000–₹3 lakh, and a custom-coded site with portals, integrations or multiple languages ₹3 lakh and up.

Price is driven by the number of unique page designs, copy and photography, the CMS and integrations, multilingual needs and SEO work. Also budget for the domain, hosting or platform fees and yearly maintenance.

items.q: Should I build a custom-coded website, or use WordPress or Webflow?
a: Use Webflow for design-led marketing sites your team edits visually, WordPress for content-heavy sites that need plugins and a familiar editor, and custom code such as Next.js when you need top performance, unusual functionality or integrations that platforms handle badly.

If the main job of the site is selling products, Shopify is usually the better default. gaa-tha recommends a platform only after scoping who will edit the site, what it must connect to and how it needs to grow.

items.q: Do you build portfolio and brand websites?
a: Yes — gaa-tha designs and builds portfolio and brand websites for founders, creative studios, professional firms, manufacturers and consumer brands, with the brand story, visual identity and copy created in-house alongside design and development.
These sites are built to load fast, show work well on mobile, rank for the business name and services, and turn visitors into enquiries through clear calls to action, forms and WhatsApp.

items.q: How much does a mobile app cost in India?
a: As an indicative 2026 Indian market range (not a quote), a simple mobile app typically costs ₹2–5 lakh, a mid-complexity app with logins, payments and an admin panel ₹5–15 lakh, and a complex app with real-time features, multiple user roles or heavy integrations ₹15 lakh and up.

Cost is driven by the number of screens and user roles, whether you need both iOS and Android, the back end and admin panel, third-party integrations and design depth. A common rule of thumb is to budget 15–20% of the build cost each year for updates, OS changes and hosting.

items.q: Should my app be built in Flutter or React Native?
a: Both Flutter and React Native build iOS and Android apps from one codebase and either is a sound choice for most business apps — Flutter is often picked for pixel-consistent custom UI and smooth animation, React Native when the team or website already uses JavaScript and React.

Choose native Swift or Kotlin only when the app depends heavily on device hardware or platform-specific features. gaa-tha recommends the stack based on your features, existing technology and who will maintain the app later.

items.q: Does my ecommerce brand need a mobile app?
a: Most ecommerce brands do not need a mobile app until they have a loyal base of repeat buyers. A fast mobile website converts first-time visitors better, while an app pays off when repeat purchases, push notifications and loyalty matter more than acquisition.

Good signals are a high repeat-order rate, frequent replenishment purchases and customers who already shop weekly on mobile. Shopify brands can start with an app builder connected to the store and move to a custom app later.

link.text: Does your brand need an app?

items.q: Do you build B2B ordering and sales-force apps?
a: Yes — gaa-tha builds B2B ordering apps and portals where dealers, distributors and retailers place repeat orders against their own price lists and credit limits, and sales-force apps where field teams log visits, take orders and record collections on the move.

These usually connect to Tally, an ERP or Shopify so orders, stock and invoices stay in sync, and can be built to work offline where connectivity is weak. They suit manufacturers, FMCG distributors and wholesalers replacing phone, WhatsApp and paper orders.

items.q: Can you build a SaaS product or MVP?
a: Yes — gaa-tha builds SaaS products and MVPs from scoping and UX design through to a working web or mobile product with user accounts, subscription billing, an admin panel and analytics.
A focused MVP typically takes 8–16 weeks to a first release. We recommend launching the smallest version that proves people will use and pay for it, then building from real usage data.

items.q: Will my new website rank on Google and appear in ChatGPT or AI answers?
a: No agency can guarantee rankings or AI citations, but a website built with clean technical SEO, fast pages, structured data and clear answer-first content is far more likely to rank on Google and be quoted by ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews.

gaa-tha builds these SEO, AEO and GEO foundations into the websites we develop — crawlable HTML, schema markup, FAQ content, internal linking and an llms.txt file — and can continue with content and search work after launch.

items.q: Who owns the website, app code and accounts after the project?
a: You should own everything — the domain, the Shopify store or hosting, the source code, app store developer accounts, analytics and ad accounts — registered in your business’s name, not the agency’s.

gaa-tha sets up accounts in the client’s name or works inside accounts you already own, and hands over code and admin access at the end of the project. If an agency will not put ownership in writing, treat it as a red flag.

items.q: What is an AI agent, and how is it different from a chatbot?
a: An AI agent is software built on a large language model such as Claude, GPT or Gemini that can plan steps and take actions in your systems — look up an order, update a CRM, draft and send a reply, create an invoice — rather than only answering questions.

A traditional chatbot follows scripted flows or answers from a fixed knowledge base, while an agent chooses which tools to use to finish a task within the permissions and approval rules you set. gaa-tha builds agents with clear limits, action logs and human hand-off so they are safe to run on real work.

items.q: What can AI agents do for a small business?
a: AI agents can take over repetitive work that mixes rules and judgement: answering customer and order-status queries, qualifying leads, following up on quotes, reading invoices and purchase orders into Tally or an ERP, writing product listings and preparing daily sales reports.
The best first projects are high-volume tasks with a clear right answer and an easy way to check the output. Start with one workflow, measure hours saved and error rates, then expand.

items.q: How much does it cost to build an AI agent in India?
a: As an indicative 2026 Indian market range (not a quote), a simple AI assistant or single-workflow automation typically costs ₹50,000–₹2 lakh to build, and a custom AI agent connected to several business systems ₹2–10 lakh or more.

On top of the build come running costs — AI model usage billed per token, hosting, and tools such as the WhatsApp Business API — which scale with volume. Build cost is driven by the number of integrations, how much data needs cleaning, accuracy and approval requirements, and the languages supported.

items.q: Which AI model is best for business — Claude, GPT or Gemini?
a: There is no single best AI model for business: Claude, GPT and Gemini are all strong, and the right choice depends on the task — reasoning over long documents, tool use, image and file input, speed, cost per request and data-residency needs.

gaa-tha tests candidate models on your real examples before choosing and builds systems so the model can be swapped as prices and capabilities change. Many production setups use a larger model for hard steps and a smaller, cheaper one for routine ones.

items.q: Is my business data safe with AI — will it be used to train models?
a: On the paid business API plans of Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (GPT) and Google (Gemini), your inputs and outputs are not used to train their models by default, which differs from some free consumer apps — check each provider’s current terms.

Safety also depends on how the system is built: send the model only the data a task needs, keep credentials and customer records in your own systems, restrict what each agent can access and log every action. That is how gaa-tha designs agents, with data-retention and regional hosting options considered for sensitive data.

items.q: What is AI workflow automation?
a: AI workflow automation connects your apps — forms, email, WhatsApp, CRM, Shopify, Google Sheets, Tally — so data moves between them automatically, with an AI model handling the steps that need reading or judgement, such as classifying an enquiry, extracting invoice details or drafting a reply.

Typical examples are routing leads to the right salesperson with a summary, turning emailed purchase orders into ERP entries and sending daily stock and sales reports. gaa-tha builds these on n8n, Make or Zapier, or in custom code when volume or security demands it.

items.q: n8n vs Make vs Zapier — which automation tool should I use?
a: Zapier is the easiest to start with and has the widest range of app connectors, Make offers visual multi-step scenarios that are often cheaper than Zapier for complex flows, and n8n is the most flexible and can be self-hosted, which suits high volumes, custom code and data that must stay on your own servers.

For a few simple automations, Zapier or Make is usually enough; for business-critical or AI-heavy workflows at volume, n8n tends to be cheaper and more controllable. All three bill differently — by task, operation or execution — so compare current pricing against your expected volume.

items.q: Which business processes should I automate first?
a: Automate first the tasks that are frequent, repetitive, rule-based and costly when they go wrong — lead capture and follow-up, order and payment notifications, data entry between Shopify, spreadsheets and Tally, invoice and purchase-order processing, and routine reports.

A simple rule: if someone copies data from one screen to another several times a day, it is a candidate. gaa-tha starts with a short process audit and ranks automations by hours saved against build effort.

items.q: Can you build a WhatsApp AI chatbot for my business?
a: Yes — gaa-tha builds WhatsApp AI chatbots on the official WhatsApp Business API that answer product and policy questions, share order status, recover abandoned carts, qualify leads and book appointments, handing over to a human with the full conversation when needed.

The bot is grounded in your own catalogue, FAQs and policies and connected to systems such as Shopify or your CRM. Meta’s policy allows business-specific assistants like these rather than general-purpose AI chatbots, and business-initiated template messages are charged under Meta’s current pricing.

items.q: Can an AI chatbot reply in Hindi, Gujarati or Hinglish?
a: Yes — current AI models understand and reply in Hindi, Gujarati, Marathi, Tamil and other Indian languages, as well as Hinglish typed in Roman script, so a chatbot can answer customers in the language they write in.

Quality varies by language and topic, so gaa-tha tests the bot on real customer messages, fixes how product names and key phrases are handled, and keeps replies short and natural. Voice notes can also be transcribed and answered where the use case needs it.

items.q: What happens if an AI chatbot or agent gives a wrong answer?
a: A well-built AI system limits wrong answers by responding only from your approved content, saying when it does not know, and handing over to a human for refunds, complaints and anything outside its scope.

gaa-tha adds guardrails, approval steps for actions that move money or change records, conversation logs and a regular review of failed answers in the first months. AI reduces support load; it does not remove the need for someone who owns the customer experience.

items.q: Does my business need an ERP?
a: Your business likely needs an ERP when stock, orders, purchases, production and accounts live in separate spreadsheets, WhatsApp groups and Tally, and the team spends hours reconciling them or cannot see real-time stock and margins.

Common triggers are selling on several channels, running more than one warehouse or outlet, manufacturing with bills of materials, or growing past the point where people can track everything in their heads. If Tally plus a few sheets still works and nobody is reconciling, an ERP can wait.

items.q: Custom ERP vs Odoo vs ERPNext vs Tally — which is right for my business?
a: Tally (TallyPrime) is accounting and GST software with basic inventory rather than a full ERP; Odoo and ERPNext are full ERPs covering inventory, purchase, sales, manufacturing and CRM; and a custom ERP fits businesses whose workflows are unusual enough that adapting a packaged ERP would cost more.

Odoo has a large app ecosystem and a paid Enterprise edition alongside its free Community edition, ERPNext is fully open source, and many Indian businesses keep Tally for accounts and sync it with the ERP. gaa-tha compares the options against your processes, number of users and budget before recommending one.

items.q: How long does ERP implementation take?
a: A focused ERP implementation for a small or mid-sized business typically takes 2–4 months, and a multi-location or manufacturing rollout with integrations 4–9 months.

The timeline depends less on the software than on process mapping, data cleaning (item masters, opening stock, customer and vendor records), integrations and user training. gaa-tha rolls out in phases, usually starting with inventory and sales, so the team uses the system early instead of waiting for a big-bang launch.

items.q: Can an ERP integrate with Shopify, Amazon, Flipkart and Tally?
a: Yes — an ERP can sync with Shopify, Amazon, Flipkart and quick commerce channels so orders flow in automatically and stock updates across every channel, and it can push invoices and payments to Tally for accounting and GST.

These integrations run through connector apps, the platforms’ APIs or middleware such as n8n, depending on volume and how real-time the sync must be. gaa-tha builds and monitors them, because a broken sync is a common cause of overselling and mismatched books.

items.q: What is system integration and custom software development?
a: System integration connects the software a business already uses — Shopify, marketplaces, CRM, ERP, Tally, payment gateways, WhatsApp — so data flows between them without manual re-entry, while custom software development builds new tools, portals or apps where no off-the-shelf product fits.
gaa-tha does both: integrations and automations first where they solve the problem, and custom web apps, dashboards and internal tools when the workflow is specific to your business.

items.q: How do I choose an AI development company?
a: Choose an AI development company that starts from your business process rather than a model or tool, can show working systems instead of demos, and explains how it measures accuracy, protects your data and keeps humans in control.

Ask who owns the prompts, code and accounts, how model costs are estimated and monitored, how failures are logged and fixed, and what support looks like after launch. gaa-tha combines AI engineering with marketing and ecommerce operations, which helps when an agent touches customers, orders or catalogues.
